name: Scalp massager

lead: A scalp massager is a handheld silicone-bristle brush or a powered vibrating head used to knead the scalp while washing or at rest. It is marketed to relax the user, loosen flakes and encourage hair growth.

It is a popular accessory in hair-loss routines, mostly to help apply minoxidil or shampoo and for comfort. The idea that it regrows hair rests largely on one small 2016 Japanese study, and it should not be expected to treat pattern baldness.

paras: The cited hypothesis is that mechanical stretching of the skin transmits force to dermal papilla cells in the subcutaneous tissue, shifting the expression of hair-cycle genes and potentially thickening existing hairs. Massage may also transiently raise scalp blood flow, though its link to hair regrowth is unproven.

The device is low risk. Overly vigorous use can irritate the scalp or break hairs, and shampooing with sharp nails or hard tools is worse. The key study had only nine healthy men, no real control group and no change in hair count, only a slight rise in hair thickness. The evidence is therefore thin, and a massager is a comfort and hygiene tool, not a baldness treatment.
